correctness.rationale: The derivative of a single logistic component is f_θ'(p)=[1+(1-p)exp(p-θ)]/(1+exp(p-θ))², bounded absolutely by 1+p/4 independent of θ on fixed witness prices; tends to 1 as θ→infinity at fixed p and is eventually strictly negative for any fixed θ. Inductively keep signs at previous 2m witness prices by adding sufficiently small ε>0; choose u>last negative witness where prior derivative lies in (-ε/4,0), and a sufficiently large new θ>u so new component derivative at u exceeds 1/2, while at θ+1 both old and new derivatives are negative. Appends a disjoint positive-to-negative interval. Each such interval contains an interior strict maximum: real-analytic nonconstant function has isolated stationary zeros, hence no flat interval; negative-to-positive gaps similarly give strict minima. Positive scaling yields unit total shares; open strict signs imply relatively open parameter region. Independent rational enclosure checked explicit valuation/weight prefixes m=1..4 at all 2m windows, finite corroboration only. No upper bound on maximum count or comparative global maximum is claimed.
